title: Waiting is the enemy
cards/0/body:
Picture a waiter who takes an order and then stands by the stove until the dish is ready. Every other table waits.

That is synchronous code: the thread waits for the network or the disk and does nothing else. A good waiter hands the order to the kitchen and goes to serve other tables. That is asynchrony.
cards/1/body:
An app with a window (WPF, WinForms, Unity) has one main thread. It draws the UI and handles clicks.

If that thread is waiting for a server, the window stops responding: clicks pile up in the queue and nobody is there to handle them.
cards/2/task: Run the synchronous version to the end. On which tick is the user's click handled?
cards/3/task: Now switch the handler to await and compare: when is the click handled?
cards/4/q: Why is the click handled almost at once with await?
cards/4/options/0: While we wait for the network, the main thread is free to work through the message queue
cards/4/explain: await releases the thread while it waits. The network is no faster; the thread just isn't sitting idle.
cards/5/body:
There are two very different things you can wait for.

I/O: network, disk, database. The hardware does the work, and the thread just waits.
Computation (CPU): compression, physics, parsing. The processor itself does the work.

async/await is mainly about the first kind: how not to hold a thread while you wait.
cards/6/q: Which of these are I/O waits? Select all that apply.
cards/6/explain: Compression and physics are CPU work. You can move them to another thread, but there is nothing to wait for.
cards/7/q: Does async/await make the server request itself faster?
cards/7/options/0: No: the request takes just as long, but the thread isn't idle
cards/7/options/2: Yes, if the server supports async
cards/7/explain: The win is that the thread does other work meanwhile: drawing the window or serving other clients.
cards/8/q: Where is a blocked main thread most noticeable?
cards/8/options/0: In a windowed app or a game: the picture freezes
cards/8/explain: At 60 frames per second a game has just 16 ms per frame. Any wait on the main thread is a freeze.
